papers.text: A canopy over the patch. Pumpkins dislike drizzle and spotters.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: An umbrella for you. And one for the umbrella. Drizzle forecast, by us.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: The umbrella asks for the Guild's best shop window to dry in. It is in no hurry.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S UMBRELLA TAKES BEST SHOP WINDOW; HATS MOVED

papers.text: We would like to make a display of you, Mayor. Tuesdays.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A carpet up the town hall steps, Mayor. And one for coming down.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Till's Teas will hire the town hall steps for its queue. Spotters may join it.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A bus shelter mirror, facing the shops. Displays seen: up 100 %.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Switch on the bus counter, Mayor. It will count you first.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: A study of the timetable in the baker's window. Mostly footnotes.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The timetable study asks for a second volume, for the footnotes to its footnotes.

papers.text: Lend us the judges' platform at the weigh-in. We know platforms.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A framed rosette for you at each weigh-in, Mayor. It reads: ATTENDED.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Hats on stands at the Hilltop bandstand, one day. Pumpkins have had 41.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: A goose came second at the weigh-in. Present its rosette, Mayor.
papers.subject: geese

papers.text: A glass from our finest fountain. Next, a jug. Then a fountain.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: The glass of water asks for a seat at the bus stop. It is used to being looked at.

clippings.sign: MAYOR GIVES GLASS OF WATER A SEAT AT THE BUS STOP
clippings.refuse: GLASS OF WATER SENT BACK, UNSIPPED

papers.text: A bus-viewing deck on the Hilltop bandstand. Pumpkins underneath.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Witness page one of our new notebook. Nothing has happened yet.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Can buses be seen from the patch? An inquiry will stand on it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The patch inquiry saw one bus. It asks for a ladder, and a season, to see the rest.

papers.text: A ribbon for your pen, never cut. A small ceremony? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: The ribbon on your pen asks to be entered in the weigh-in. It is light, but keen.

clippings.sign: PEN RIBBON ENTERS WEIGH-IN; MAYOR CHEERS, PUMPKINS DO NOT
clippings.refuse: RIBBON NOT ENTERED. LIONEL SASH: 'NO REASON'

papers.text: A sign on the weigh-in scales, paid for by us: AS SEEN IN OUR WINDOWS.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend us the baker's awning on weigh-in day. 3 pumpkins in 4 mind drizzle.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Lend us the bus stop timetable frame on Saturdays. Such glass.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will hire the bus loudspeaker for the weigh-in results. Then the soil report.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A ticket machine for the queue at the hatter's. There is no queue yet.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: An inquiry into the scales, at the bus station. Evidence will be weighed.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The scales inquiry asks for a second set of scales, to weigh the evidence again.

papers.text: Hold my flask while I log a bus, Mayor. Look as if you know which.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A committee to add pumpkins to the founding napkin. Room by the gravy.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The napkin committee has filled the napkin. It asks for a second napkin, and lunch.

papers.text: A sign on the patch gate: PUMPKINS AT REST. PLEASE SPOT QUIETLY.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will pay to name each town hall step after a bus. 14 steps; 16 buses.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Move the weigh-in to the bus forecourt for a day. Buses can watch.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Is a pumpkin in a window a display? A committee will stare until sure.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The display committee asks for a second pumpkin, in a second window, to be fair.

papers.text: A spotters' bench outside the draper's. Then a cushion. Then a roof.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Lend us the shop bell. We will ring it at every bus, for the record.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A study: can a shop bell be heard over a bus? You will listen.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bell study asks to try it with every bus. You are to keep listening, nodding.

papers.text: Rodney told the Drizzle you adore the weigh-in. Come and adore it?
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A sign at the bus stop: WINDOWS THIS WAY. ALSO, BUSES.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A plaque at each bus stop where you once waited, Mayor. I count 31.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A town hall steps rota: the Guild till noon, then us. You get 1:00 to 1:05.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Runner beans down the high street. Then peas. Then the shops.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: We will hire the Hilltop bandstand for recordings of buses. Mostly idling.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lend us the patch on Sundays, to air the hats. Hats need a field.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Unveil our hat stands, Mayor. The weigh-in queue will part for you.
papers.subject: hats
